summary: PYER consists of an app where you can visualize on a map the distribution of different marine species from the Gulf of California and even the distribution probability these species will have in 2030, 2050, 2070 and 2100 based on three different oceanographic variables: Sea Surface Temperature (SST), chlorophyll (chl-a) and Particulate Organic Carbon (POC). Using the app is easy and self-intuitive, including a retro aesthetic that is friendly with the user. The marine species data preloaded in the app are socially and economically important, but the user may analyse any interest species, allowing people from different profiles to make more efficient decisions on the use for these natural resources. This app was made based on statistical analysis from NASA's MODIS-Aqua resources, using QGIS's raster calculator and integrating species observational data from iNaturalist and OBIS. The distribution predictions are made with the Maxent model. The app script was made using Copilot and Claude AIs. We hope this tool will reach a social and human positive impact, as users make the best out from the data provided in research or sustainability.
details: PYER means Prediction per Year of Expected Redistributions, and we proudly want to announce that the name is pretty self-explanatory for our project. PYER consists of an app where you can visualize on a map the distribution of different marine species from the Gulf of California and even the distribution probability these species will have based on three different oceanographic variables, being: Sea Surface Temperature (SST, in Celsius degree), chlorophyll (chl-a in mg/cm3) and Particulate Organic Carbon (POC in mg/cm3). The prediction is calculated per each pixel on the map and based on significant statistical linear regressions to find tendencies for the years 2030, 2050, 2070 and 2100, selected due to the UN's 2030 Agenda, mid-century and subsequent decades. Also the marine species data preloaded in the app are socially and economically important for tourism, sportsfishing and commercial fishing, but the user can upload any archive with .cvs extension based on species observations in the Gulf of California.
